questions.question: You’re at a party and someone spills their drink on your new jacket. What would be the most appropriate way to respond?
options: Don’t worry about it, it’s not your fault.
I’m sorry to hear that—let me buy you a new jacket!
You should have been more careful with your drink.
It’s okay, I’ll just throw it away.
questions.answer: Don’t worry about it, it’s not your fault.

questions.question: Your colleague suggests, *'Let’s try this new café downtown—it’s supposed to be amazing!'* What would be the most polite way to respond if you’re not interested?
options: No, I don’t think I’ll go—it sounds too loud.
I’m afraid I can’t, but thanks for the suggestion!
Yeah, that sounds great! I’ll go with you!
Actually, I’ve already decided to go to the gym instead.
questions.answer: I’m afraid I can’t, but thanks for the suggestion!

questions.question: A friend asks, *'Have you ever tried veganism? It’s so healthy!'* How would you politely express an opinion that it’s not for everyone?
options: Yes, I’ve tried it and it’s definitely good for you.
I’ve thought about it, but I don’t think everyone can or wants to eat like that.
I’ll definitely give it a go next week!
No, I don’t eat meat at all, so I can’t comment.
questions.answer: I’ve thought about it, but I don’t think everyone can or wants to eat like that.

questions.question: In a formal email to a client, you want to suggest a follow-up meeting. Which of these would be the most professional?
options: I’d love to meet up again soon—let’s grab coffee!
Could we arrange another meeting to discuss the project further?
Sure, I’ll call you tomorrow to fix a time.
I’m not sure if we should meet again—maybe next week?
questions.answer: Could we arrange another meeting to discuss the project further?

questions.question: Your boss asks you to help with a last-minute presentation. What would be the most appropriate way to respond if you’re unsure whether you can take on the extra work?
options: Of course! I’ll make sure to finish it by tomorrow.
I’m sorry, I’m really busy right now—could I ask someone else?
I’d be happy to help, but I’ll need to check my schedule first.
No, I don’t think I can do that—it’s too much work.
questions.answer: I’d be happy to help, but I’ll need to check my schedule first.
